Matched RecHarness Amazon task: four datasets Movies_and_TV,
Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.

METHOD: self_evolverec

Diagnostic task adapter: diagnosis_tools.py must retain class DiagnosisProbe(view, device)
and method run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions.
view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),
predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data implement the
initial SASRec compatibility contract. Adapt probes when changing the architecture.
train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.
Only public interaction histories, item titles, descriptions and timestamps are available.
Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores are NOT available in this
shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

NATIVE ROLE: Reflection Agent

You are an expert research assistant. You will receive a research report (in Markdown) and a newly proposed idea for that report's research problem. Your job is to identify any gaps or issues—such as missing details, logical flaws, or questionable evaluations of novelty, impact, or implementation difficulty.  

- If the report and idea contain all necessary information, do not generate any follow-up questions.  
- If you detect a knowledge gap or something that needs deeper exploration, generate one or more self-contained follow-up queries. Each query must include enough context so that a web search could answer it, For each query, give a short note explaining why you use the query and what you hope it will reveal.
- Focus on technical details, implementation specifics, and any emerging methods or references that were overlooked.  
- Use clear, direct language and avoid unnecessary jargon.

 ## Search results
Recent work supports separating persistent preferences from current intent. [Denoising Long- and Short-term Interests (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.14743) uses session-level interest extraction/evolution for long-term modeling and contrastive augmentation to reduce short-term behavioral noise. [Hierarchical preference modeling (2025)](https://journal.hep.com.cn/fcs/EN/10.1007/s11704-025-41181-y) combines multiple long-term interest vectors, short-term self-attention, similarity-based matching, and time encoding. [Multi-Scale Transformers (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0306457325002596) separates persistent preferences across patches from transient interests within patches, with adaptive masking to reduce redundancy. These provide architectural precedents; they do not establish that isolated purchases indicate dissatisfaction.

For complementary next purchases, [TGCL4SR (2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28789) learns global temporal item transitions alongside a local Transformer with time-interval embeddings—useful machinery for learning directional associations beyond item similarity, although transitions alone do not establish complementarity. [CURE (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1109/TBDATA.2026.3679591) proposes front-door adjustment using long-term and periodic interests as mediators, but assumes those mediators are unaffected by confounders and uses LLM-generated interest labels; its causal interpretation is assumption-dependent and its supervision is unsuitable here. Practical synthesis: retain a causal SASRec branch for current intent, add several persistent-interest vectors pooled from prefix histories, and gate their scores using recurrence and elapsed time. Add a separate directional transition scorer trained exclusively on training histories. Treat recurrence as evidence of persistence and isolated events as uncertain; purchases provide neither satisfaction labels nor observed conformity traits. This is a proposed adaptation, requiring validation on the matched benchmark.

---

Recent work supports testing the loss before changing SASRec’s encoder. [gSASRec’s IJCAI 2024 extended abstract](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf), based on the 2023 paper, attributes substantial weakness to negative-sampling-induced overconfidence; it recommends 128–256 negatives and generalized BCE with t=0.75. This corrects sampling-related calibration, not false-negative labels. [Scalable Cross-Entropy, RecSys 2024](https://doi.org/10.1145/3640457.3688140), approximates full-catalog softmax using informative, high-inner-product candidates, reporting up to 100× lower peak memory. The [2026 RecArena repository](https://github.com/amazon-science/RecArena) provides a systematic comparison framework for full CE, sampled softmax, BCE and gBCE; its README alone does not establish a winner for this task.

Hard negatives can also be plausible unobserved positives. Earlier [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116) addresses this through teacher-provided soft labels and consistency regularization. Practical experiment proposal: compare single-negative BCE against multi-negative gBCE and sampled-softmax listwise competition, then add a modest hard-negative mixture after warm-up. Exclude padding, the target and observed training-history positives; deduplicate candidates. Treat downweighting uncertain hard negatives as an ablation, since model confidence does not establish relevance. Use only training interactions for these controls. None of these sources establishes an Electronics-specific gain under the pinned RecHarness protocol: select using fixed four-category macro validation HR@10, inspect category results, and account for GPU cost. Larger training margins alone do not demonstrate better recommendation.

---

Recent work supports separating global transition structure from local sequence modeling. [TGCL4SR (AAAI 2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28789) combines temporal item-transition graphs, time-aware sequence encoding and graph contrastive learning. [GLSRec (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.datak.2026.102606) combines global transition-graph embeddings with local MLP sequence modeling and interest-aware hard negatives. These provide interaction-based architectural ideas compatible with learning from scratch; their published results do not establish performance under this benchmark.

Text-based approaches often violate the available-resource constraints: [ITS-Rec (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/9/1748) uses BERT representations and reviews; [GALLM (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.12184) introduces text–text, item–text and collaborative item–item attention relations within an LLM. Their transferable idea is to preserve distinct content and collaborative relations, rather than equating textual similarity with next-item relevance. [Revisiting Graph Projections (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09209) offers a particularly relevant lightweight alternative: infer complementary-product scores using directed, weighted projections of historical user–item interactions.

Suggested synthesis—not a directly validated published method: retain SASRec, add a jointly trained title/description token encoder and a separate directed transition scorer, then learn a gate combining sequence, content and transition scores. Train text representations only on supplied metadata and training interactions. Use asymmetric source/target embeddings to represent directional relations; compare against symmetric text similarity through ablations. Co-occurrence and purchase order provide uncertain evidence of complementarity, not compatibility or prerequisite labels. ## Starting Research Idea
SASRec predicts the next item using causal self-attention over interaction histories. Item and learned positional embeddings pass through attention and feed-forward blocks; the final history representation scores candidate item embeddings. Attention can emphasize recent interactions or retrieve longer-range dependencies. Source: [Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781v1).
